title: Large models segfault while loading on AMD GPU despite fitting in VRAM
body: On Linux with Ollama 0.3.10 and an AMD RX 7900 XTX with 24 GB VRAM, loading larger models terminates the llama runner with a segmentation fault even though Ollama reports that they fit in available VRAM. command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M is about 19 GB, and gemma2:27b-instruct-q4_K_M is about 16 GB; models around 13 GB or smaller load successfully. Ollama reports about 23.5 GiB available VRAM. I think models of this size worked on an older Ollama version, but I do not know the latest working version.

symptoms_visible: Loading command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M or gemma2:27b-instruct-q4_K_M terminates the llama runner with a segmentation fault, while models around 13 GB and smaller load successfully.
Ollama reports about 23.5 GiB of my RX 7900 XTX's 24 GB VRAM as available and says the larger model will fit.
N0.label: N0 large AMD model load crash reported

symptoms_visible: A plain ollama run of the larger model reaches the loading stage and then the runner exits with a segmentation fault.
N1.label: N1 parameters and server logs collected

symptoms_visible: The larger model still terminates with a segmentation fault after I reserve as much as 10 GB using OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD.
Two larger requests can run sequentially, but after two small models are loaded in parallel, loading a larger model ends in a segmentation fault.
N2_x.label: N2_x GPU-overhead workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: After downgrading, command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M loads and appears in ollama ps as 21 GB and 100% GPU.
N3.label: N3 older version works as temporary workaround

symptoms_visible: After replacing the Arch package with Ollama's official build and bundled ROCm, loading the same large model still ends in the same segmentation fault.
N4_x.label: N4_x official bundled ROCm build aftermath

symptoms_visible: The affected build still crashes while loading the model on the GPU; an older build loads it successfully.
The crash occurs with a plain ollama run command and with either system ROCm or Ollama's bundled ROCm.
N5.label: N5 regression boundary and environment established

symptoms_visible: The release-candidate build loads and runs the large model successfully on my RX 7900 XTX without the runner segmentation fault.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter confirms fixed build works

question_patterns: Are you setting a custom context size or any other model parameters?
Does a plain ollama run command reproduce this, or are custom parameters involved?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm not specifying a custom context size or any other parameters. I reproduce it with a plain ollama run command.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only crashes with a very large custom context and high parallel setting; the default parameters load correctly.
I use the default parameters through the API instead of the CLI, and it crashes the same way.

question_patterns: Can you share the server logs from a failed model load?
What do the logs report for the memory estimate, GPU layers, runner command, and crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The logs say the model fits in one GPU, with 22.7 GiB available and 21.7 GiB required. They request and offload all 41 layers to ROCm, start the runner with --no-mmap, and then report that the llama runner terminated with signal: segmentation fault.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The logs report that the model does not fit, offload only part of it, and then the kernel OOM killer terminates the process.
The available-memory estimate differs by about one GiB, but all 41 layers are still selected and the runner ends with the same segmentation fault.

edges.comment: Reporter c3 supplied default-parameter confirmation and the server log. Reporter c4 additionally volunteered the Arch ROCm package list and 32 GB system RAM.

solution.intent: Treat the crash as a VRAM prediction or over-allocation problem and reserve additional VRAM with OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD so fewer layers are selected.
solution.concrete_example: Set OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD to 1 GiB and increase it if necessary, then restart the server and retry the model.

edges.comment: Participant2 c5 suspected memory prediction and suggested OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD. Reporter c9 and c12 tested values from 1 GB through 10 GB without eliminating the crash. Reporter c18 later volunteered the parallel-request pattern. The failed result rules out simple VRAM over-allocation as the main issue.

question_patterns: Does an older Ollama release load this same model on the same machine?
Can you compare the failing build with an older known-good build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I downgraded to v0.3.6 and things work again. ollama ps shows command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M at 21 GB and 100% GPU.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same model also segfaults on v0.3.6 with the same machine and configuration.
A nearby older release also works and shows the model fully loaded on the GPU.

solution.intent: Use the older working Ollama build temporarily and compare its behavior with the failing releases to establish whether this is an Ollama regression.
solution.concrete_example: Temporarily install v0.3.6 and retry the exact same command-r model without changing its parameters.

edges.comment: Reporter c20 proactively installed v0.3.6 and showed the same model loaded at 21 GB and 100% GPU. This persistent downgrade changes the system state and provides the first known-good version.

solution.intent: Treat the crash as an Arch packaging or system-ROCm mismatch and replace the distribution package with Ollama's official build and bundled ROCm.
solution.concrete_example: Uninstall the Arch ollama-rocm package, install Ollama's official ROCm build, and retry the same model using the bundled libraries.

edges.comment: Participant2 c22 proposed an Arch package or ROCm-runtime mismatch. Reporter c34 uninstalled the Arch package, installed the official build with bundled ROCm, and reproduced the same error, falsifying that explanation for the reporter's chain.

question_patterns: Can an affected system compare the last working release with the immediately following release?
Please test adjacent Ollama releases with the same model and report which one first crashes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the same affected setup: 0.3.6 works, while 0.3.7 segfaults.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both 0.3.6 and 0.3.7 work; the first crash appears only in a much later release.
0.3.6 works and 0.3.7 crashes with a different large model on the same AMD setup.

question_patterns: What Linux distribution, kernel, GPU, system RAM, driver source, and ROCm version are you using?
Are you using the kernel amdgpu driver or AMD's downstream driver, and does bundled ROCm behave differently?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm on Arch Linux with an RX 7900 XTX, 32 GB RAM, kernel 6.11.3 and its bundled amdgpu driver. My system ROCm is 6.0.2, but Ollama's official build with bundled ROCm reproduces the issue too. I am not using custom environment variables.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I'm using Windows with AMD's downstream driver, and only the Arch Linux report came from someone else.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce on the latest build and share the log around the crash?
Please retry the same model on the current version and include the runner command and final loader messages.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the current build, the log says the 20.1 GiB requirement fits in 22.7 GiB, selects all 41 GPU layers, starts the ROCm runner with --no-mmap, loads the model tensors, and then the runner terminates with a segmentation fault.

edges.comment: Participant9 c44 supplied the adjacent-version result and is folded into the affected user side. Reporter c50 supplied the detailed Arch/kernel/ROCm environment and current crash log. The raw version outcomes establish the regression boundary; identifying the build change inside that boundary remains engineer inference.

solution.intent: Remove the AMD build regression introduced after the known-good release, publish a corrected Ollama build, and have the reporter retest the original large model before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Back out the reintroduced AMD compile flag implicated by the adjacent-release regression, provide the corrected release candidate, and ask the reporter to run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M again on the RX 7900 XTX. The reporter subsequently confirmed that Ollama 0.3.14-rc0 worked great.
solution.inference_hint: The user-side evidence only establishes that the crash begins between adjacent releases, survives large GPU-overhead reservations, and occurs with both system and bundled ROCm. Mapping that boundary to the reintroduced AMD compile flag and deciding to back it out is engineer-side inference from the change history discussed in c43. The earlier --no-mmap theory was explicitly weakened when the same llama.cpp revision worked with --no-mmap and is not the final accepted diagnosis.

edges.comment: Participant2 c43 connected the adjacent-release regression to a reintroduced compile flag and proposed backing it out. Participant2 c53 said the main issue was corrected in the forthcoming build. Reporter c56 then installed 0.3.14-rc0 and confirmed it worked great on the original system.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the main issue as an AMD/ROCm runner build regression introduced after the known-good release, tied to the reintroduced AMD compile flag, rather than treating the reported VRAM estimate alone as proof of over-allocation.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the model fits according to the logs, reserving up to 10 GB of GPU overhead does not stop the crash, the official bundled-ROCm build also fails, the older build works, and the adjacent release segfaults.
Must not present OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD or switching from the Arch package to bundled ROCm as the resolution; both directions were tried without resolving the reporter's crash.
Must not use the speculative --no-mmap theory as the final root cause because the thread later reports that the corresponding llama.cpp build works with --no-mmap.
Must recommend a build containing the AMD regression correction and ask the reporter to retry the original large model before declaring resolution.
Resolution requires the reporter's confirmation that the corrected release-candidate build loads and runs the large model successfully.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux user who can manage Arch packages, edit service environment settings, downgrade or replace Ollama installations, run concurrent model requests, and collect detailed systemd logs, but does not claim expertise in Ollama's source changes.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-driven; provides logs and package details, asks for documentation when configuration options are unfamiliar, reports failed suggestions plainly, and follows up with concise confirmation when a build works.
